newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Gov. urges support for school funding reform.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Gov. urges support for school funding reform.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar on Tuesday urged suburban Chicago officials to support a school funding reform plan that would provide "substantial" property tax relief.

Speaking at a luncheon in Oak Brook, Ill., the Republican governor told mayors and managers from DuPage County governments that he was counting on them to help convince legislators "that this is the year for them to make good on their campaign promises to make school funding fairer and more equitable."

"The need for this reform is evident. Nearly 60 cents of every dollar spent on education come from property taxes," Edgar said. "We also have 700,000 students in this state who are not supported by an adequate level of funding."
Edgar called for increased state support to provide at least $1 billion in property tax relief and to maintain a miminum school funding level of $4,225 per pupil.

"Additional state dollars will be needed primarily to replace local property tax dollars," the governor said. "I believe the fairest way to raise those dollars is through the income tax, but I am open to other possibilities."

Last year, Edgar's push for a constitutional amendment requiring the state to fund at least 50 percent of education costs failed to win support in the General Assembly. This year, the governor has said he would focus on achieving a legislative solution to school funding.
